subject.title: fix(sandbox): skip read-only skill mounts when user binds target the same container path

question: Should an explicitly allowed user bind to a protected skill destination retain any break-glass override semantics, or must protected read-only skill mounts always take precedence?
rationale: The branch resolves the Docker startup failure, but it also selects a lasting compatibility and sandbox-boundary policy for an existing user configuration; source-level review cannot safely infer that product/security contract.

options.title: Keep protected mounts authoritative
options.body: Adopt the branch's precedence rule, clearly surface the ignored bind, and add upgrade/config documentation plus coverage for explicitly allowed reserved targets.

options.title: Preserve break-glass override semantics
options.body: Define and implement a deliberate override path for explicitly permitted reserved destinations instead of silently dropping the configured bind.

recommendation.title: Keep protected mounts authoritative
recommendation.body: Adopt the branch's precedence rule, clearly surface the ignored bind, and add upgrade/config documentation plus coverage for explicitly allowed reserved targets.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a repository-level sandbox security and compatibility decision, and the PR timeline specifically routed the discussion to this person.
